chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, who said:
Im al-Rida (peace be upon him) was asked about the speckled crow, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not to be eaten.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'And who permitted to you the black (one)?'

key_terms.يُؤْكَلُ: To be eaten / Permissible to consume

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating speckled and black crows according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes the impermissibility of consuming the speckled crow (*al-ghurab al-abqa*), while rhetorically questioning the permissibility of the black crow, highlighting a nuanced scholarly debate on avian classification. This reflects the Shia juristic approach of distinguishing between specific animal types based on prophetic tradition and logical deduction regarding their nature. The inquiry underscores the importance of precise identification in dietary laws, a key concern in Shia fiqh.
